root_cause: Router sub-interface Gi0/0.10 is administratively shut down, removing the VLAN 10 default gateway
evidence: show output: 'GigabitEthernet0/0.10 is administratively down, line protocol is down'
fix_steps: Enter interface Gi0/0.10 configuration mode
Run 'no shutdown'
Confirm status shows up/up in show ip interface brief
Re-test PC1 to Server1 connectivity

root_cause: DHCP pool LAN_POOL is exhausted (10/10 leased), so new clients fall back to APIPA
evidence: show output: 'ip dhcp pool LAN_POOL; total addresses 10; leased 10; zero available'
fix_steps: Enlarge the DHCP pool network/mask or add a second pool
Clear stale leases with 'clear ip dhcp binding *' if leases are orphaned
Release/renew IP on PC2
Verify PC2 receives an address in the correct subnet

root_cause: DNS lookups fail because 'ip name-server 192.168.1.5' is present but domain lookup / DNS service is not active on the client's gateway
evidence: show output: 'no ip domain-lookup; ip name-server 192.168.1.5 not active'
fix_steps: Enable domain lookups with 'ip domain-lookup' if the router is meant to resolve names
Confirm DNS server 192.168.1.5 is reachable and actually serving
Verify client is receiving the correct DNS server via DHCP or static config
Re-test 'nslookup google.com' from PC1

root_cause: OSPF hello-interval mismatch (R1=10, R2=20) prevents adjacency
evidence: show output: 'R1: ip ospf hello-interval 10; R2: ip ospf hello-interval 20'
fix_steps: Set matching hello-interval on both routers
Ensure dead-interval is 4x hello-interval on both sides
Confirm neighbor reaches FULL state with 'show ip ospf neighbor'

root_cause: Extended ACL 101 has a deny statement for the Sales subnet to the web server ahead of/instead of a permit for tcp port 80
evidence: show output: 'access-list 101 deny tcp 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.10 eq 80'
fix_steps: Review full ACL 101 for an intended permit statement
Add/reorder a permit tcp ... eq 80 line above the deny, or remove the deny if unintended
Re-apply ACL if statement order changed
Re-test HTTP access from Sales subnet

root_cause: NAT source list is applied without the 'overload' keyword, so PAT is not enabled and only one internal host can use the public IP at a time
evidence: show output: 'ip nat inside source list 1 interface Gi0/1 (missing overload keyword)'
fix_steps: Re-enter the NAT statement with the 'overload' keyword
Verify 'ip nat inside'/'ip nat outside' are applied to correct interfaces
Clear existing translations if needed
Re-test internet access from multiple internal PCs

root_cause: GUEST_ACL permits all IP traffic from the guest subnet to any destination, allowing guest Wi-Fi to reach internal private servers
evidence: show output: 'GUEST_ACL: 10 permit ip 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255 any'
fix_steps: Add explicit deny statements for internal server subnets above the permit any
Restrict permit statement to only Internet-bound destinations
Re-apply ACL to the guest VLAN interface
Verify guest clients can reach Internet but not internal servers

root_cause: VLAN 20 is missing from the trunk's allowed VLAN list between SW1 and SW2
evidence: show output: 'Switchport trunk allowed vlan 10 30 40' (VLAN 20 not listed)
fix_steps: On both switch ends, run 'switchport trunk allowed vlan add 20'
Verify with 'show interfaces trunk' that VLAN 20 now shows as allowed
Re-test VLAN 20 connectivity across the trunk

root_cause: Likely a DNS resolution issue preventing gateway reachability check
evidence: show output: 'IP configuration shows Default Gateway 192.168.1.254 on Host'
fix_steps: Check DNS server reachability from PC3
Flush DNS cache on PC3
Retry ping to gateway

root_cause: Management SVI (VLAN 1 interface) on SW1 is administratively shut down, blocking SSH access
evidence: show output: 'interface Vlan1; ip address 192.168.1.2 255.255.255.0; shutdown'
fix_steps: Enter interface Vlan1 configuration mode
Run 'no shutdown'
Confirm status is up/up
Re-test SSH access to 192.168.1.2

root_cause: The inter-switch link between SW1 and SW2 is configured as access mode instead of trunk, blocking VLAN 10 traffic between switches
evidence: show output: 'SW1 Fa0/24: switchport mode access; SW2 Fa0/24: switchport mode access'
fix_steps: On both switches, run 'switchport mode trunk' on Fa0/24
Allow VLAN 10 (and others as needed) on the trunk
Verify trunk state with 'show interfaces trunk'
Re-test PC1 to PC2 connectivity

root_cause: Serial0/1/0 is configured as a passive-interface under OSPF while it is meant to be an active routing link to R1, so routes are not being exchanged
evidence: show output: 'router ospf 1; network 10.0.0.0 0.255.255.255 area 0; passive-interface Serial0/1/0'
fix_steps: Remove passive-interface status for Serial0/1/0 with 'no passive-interface Serial0/1/0'
Confirm OSPF neighbor forms on that link
Verify R2 now shows Head Office routes in 'show ip route'

root_cause: Trunk link between the access switch and distribution switch is likely misconfigured, blocking VLAN 40 traffic
evidence: show output: 'interface FastEthernet0/10; switchport access vlan 14'
fix_steps: Check trunk allowed-VLAN list for VLAN 40
Re-add VLAN 40 to the trunk if pruned
Re-test connectivity to Finance Server

root_cause: Branch router R2's LAN interface is missing 'ip helper-address', so DHCP Discover broadcasts are not relayed to the central DHCP server
evidence: show output: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0; ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0' with no helper-address configured
fix_steps: Add 'ip helper-address <DHCP-server-IP>' under Gi0/0
Confirm relay works with a test client DHCP request
Verify client receives correct subnet address

root_cause: Static route's next-hop IP address (10.0.0.5) is not a valid/reachable address, causing intermittent packet loss for 172.16.0.0/16 traffic
evidence: show output: 'ip route 172.16.0.0 255.255.0.0 10.0.0.5 (Next-hop IP 10.0.0.5 unreachable)'
fix_steps: Confirm the correct next-hop IP for the R2 link
Correct the static route with the valid next-hop
Verify route appears correctly in 'show ip route'
Re-test end-to-end connectivity

root_cause: ACL 100 permits FTP data connections but is missing the control-channel permit for TCP port 21, so FTP sessions time out
evidence: show output: 'access-list 100 permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.25 eq 20' (port 21 absent)
fix_steps: Add 'permit tcp 192.168.1.0 0.0.0.255 host 10.0.0.25 eq 21' to the ACL
Keep the existing port 20 entry for active-mode data connections
Re-apply the ACL if needed
Re-test FTP connection

root_cause: Static NAT mapping is defined but Gi0/0 is missing the 'ip nat inside' designation, so translation never triggers
evidence: show output: 'ip nat inside source static 192.168.1.100 203.0.113.10; interface Gi0/0 missing ip nat inside'
fix_steps: Apply 'ip nat inside' on Gi0/0 (the internal-facing interface)
Confirm 'ip nat outside' is applied on the WAN-facing interface
Verify translation with 'show ip nat translations'
Re-test access to the public IP from outside

root_cause: RADIUS shared secret configured on the WLC/router does not match the RADIUS server's configured secret, so authentication requests are rejected
evidence: show output: 'radius-server host 10.0.0.50 key incorrect_secret_key'
next_command: debug radius authentication (lab only) or show run | include radius-server
fix_steps: Confirm the correct shared secret configured on the RADIUS server
Update the key on the WLC/router to match exactly (case-sensitive)
Re-test wireless client authentication

root_cause: Native VLAN mismatch between SW1 (VLAN 10) and SW2 (VLAN 99) on the trunk link generates warnings and can leak untagged traffic
evidence: show output: 'SW1: switchport trunk native vlan 10; SW2: switchport trunk native vlan 99'
fix_steps: Set the same native VLAN on both trunk ends
Verify native VLAN mismatch warnings clear in the logs
Confirm trunk is fully operational

root_cause: The configured default gateway (10.1.1.30) falls outside the client's /28 subnet (10.1.1.48-10.1.1.63 or similar), so off-subnet traffic cannot be routed
evidence: show output: 'IP 10.1.1.50 mask 255.255.255.240; Gateway 10.1.1.30 (Outside subnet boundary)'
next_command: show ip interface brief on gateway router; ipconfig on host
fix_steps: Recalculate the correct subnet range for 10.1.1.50/28
Reconfigure the client (or DHCP scope) with a gateway address inside that range
Re-test connectivity to hosts outside the local subnet

root_cause: OSPF process ID mismatch between routers is preventing route redistribution from taking effect
evidence: show output: 'router ospf 1; redistribute eigrp 100'
fix_steps: Verify OSPF process IDs match on all routers
Re-check EIGRP AS number 100 is correct
Re-test route visibility

root_cause: Outbound ACL OUTBOUND only permits TCP port 80, so HTTPS (443) traffic is implicitly denied
evidence: show output: 'access-list OUTBOUND permit tcp any any eq 80' (443 absent)
fix_steps: Add 'permit tcp any any eq 443' to the ACL
Re-apply if needed on the correct interface/direction
Re-test HTTPS access from internal users

root_cause: Host A and Host B are statically configured with the same IP address, causing a duplicate address conflict on the LAN
evidence: show output: 'Log: %IP-4-DUP_ADDR: Duplicate address 192.168.1.100 on FastEthernet0/1'
next_command: show arp / show ip arp inspection
fix_steps: Identify which host should keep 192.168.1.100
Reassign a unique IP to the other host
Clear ARP caches on affected devices
Verify the duplicate address log entry stops recurring

root_cause: VTP password mismatch between SW1 and SW2 is blocking VTP updates
evidence: show output: 'SW1: vtp domain CORP; SW2: vtp domain corp'
fix_steps: Set matching VTP passwords on both switches
Re-check VTP status
Re-test VLAN propagation

root_cause: The uplink trunk port is not marked as a trusted interface for Dynamic ARP Inspection, so legitimate ARP replies from upstream devices are being dropped
evidence: show output: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/1; ip arp inspection trust missing on uplink'
fix_steps: Configure 'ip arp inspection trust' on the uplink interface
Leave DAI enabled/untrusted on access ports facing end hosts
Verify legitimate ARP traffic is no longer dropped

root_cause: Port security on Fa0/10 has reached its maximum MAC address limit (1) and a second device triggered a security violation, putting the port into err-disabled state
evidence: show output: 'Log: %PORT_SECURITY-2-PSECURE_VIOLATION: Security violation occurred on port Fa0/10'
fix_steps: Identify why a second MAC appeared (new device, hub, or a NIC/MAC change)
Remove the offending device or raise the max MAC count if legitimate
Re-enable the port with 'shutdown' then 'no shutdown' (or errdisable recovery)
Confirm the port returns to connected state

root_cause: R2's HSRP priority (100) is too close to R1's (110), causing flapping between Active and Standby
evidence: show output: 'R1: standby 1 priority 110 hello 3; R2: standby 1 priority 100 hello 10'
fix_steps: Increase the priority gap between R1 and R2
Enable preempt on R1
Re-test failover stability

root_cause: Sub-interface Gi0/0.20 is missing the 'encapsulation dot1Q 20' statement, so it cannot process tagged VLAN 20 frames
evidence: show output: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0.20; ip address 192.168.20.1 255.255.255.0' (encapsulation dot1Q 20 absent)
fix_steps: Add 'encapsulation dot1Q 20' under the sub-interface
Confirm the sub-interface shows the correct encapsulation with 'show interfaces Gi0/0.20'
Re-test inter-VLAN routing for VLAN 20

root_cause: IPv6 Router Advertisements are suppressed on Gi0/0, so SLAAC clients never receive prefix information needed for address autoconfiguration
evidence: show output: 'interface GigabitEthernet0/0; ipv6 nd suppress-ra enabled'
fix_steps: Remove suppression with 'no ipv6 nd suppress-ra'
Confirm RAs are being sent with a packet capture or 'debug ipv6 nd' in lab
Verify clients receive a global IPv6 address via SLAAC

root_cause: CDP is disabled globally on the device, so no neighbor information is being advertised or learned
evidence: show output: 'no cdp run globally active in running configuration'
fix_steps: Enable CDP globally with 'cdp run'
Confirm the interface also has CDP enabled (not 'no cdp enable')
Verify neighbors appear in 'show cdp neighbors'
